top_stories.title: Grok 4.6 hits frontier performance at ~60% lower cost, with 4.7 promised in weeks
points: xAI's Grok 4.6 scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (a composite benchmark of reasoning, coding and knowledge tests), matching OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and trailing only Anthropic's Fable 5 (62) and Opus 5 (63).
Pricing is $2 per 1M input tokens and $6 per 1M output tokens (tokens are the chunks of text/code a model processes), undercutting frontier rivals by roughly 60%.
Agent efficiency is the headline metric: on AA-Briefcase tests Grok needed ~53 turns and 0.5B input tokens versus Claude Opus 5 Max's ~103 turns and 2.0B tokens, measured at $0.84 per task.
Available now in Cursor, Grok Build, the API, OpenRouter, Vercel and Cloudflare, with 2x free usage for the first week and a $30/month SuperGrok consumer plan.
Elon Musk called it 'objectively No. 1 when considering intelligence, speed & cost' and says Grok 4.7 lands in 3-4 weeks and will 'exceed all current models.'

unique_angles.point: Grok 4.7 will reportedly integrate SpaceX company data.
Cost per task is unchanged from Grok 4.5, putting a frontier model in the same price band as open-source Chinese models — though Musk's timelines warrant skepticism.
The Cursor/xAI partnership adds distribution pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic to rethink pricing and release timing.

top_stories.title: Claude in Chrome gains full Cowork sessions and live web control
points: Anthropic's Chrome side panel now runs a full Cowork session (its agentic desktop workspace) that syncs conversation history, Skills, connectors and multi-step tasks between browser and Claude apps.
The agent can click, type and scan live web pages, giving Claude real-time internet access for research and data gathering.
Sessions persist across devices; the feature is rolling out on paid Anthropic plans.

top_stories.title: Lovable raises $400M at $13.3B as AI app-layer funding accelerates
points: Lovable's $400M round values the AI coding/no-code platform at $13.3B, more than doubling its December 2025 valuation.
Cognition is in talks at a $40B valuation after crossing $1B in annualized revenue run rate (current monthly revenue extrapolated over a year).

unique_angles.point: Mistral launched regional inference and third-party open-model hosting, backed by a European compute coalition targeting 1 gigawatt (1 billion watts) by 2030.

top_stories.title: DeepSeek V4-Pro undercuts rivals by ~10x on price
points: DeepSeek quietly shipped V4-Pro-0813 at $0.435 per 1M input tokens and $0.87 per 1M output tokens — roughly one-tenth the cost of comparable frontier models.
Benchmarks are reported as frontier-comparable, beating Opus 4.8 on coding, benchmarking and automation tasks.

top_stories.title: Enterprise AI shifts from assistant to agentic delegation
points: OpenAI data shows the highest-usage firms now generate 8-10x more output tokens per active user than typical enterprises, up from 2.6x, and adopt connected tools far more often.
Adoption is moving from AI-as-assistant to agentic delegation, where agents autonomously complete multi-step work under human oversight.
Verification and quality assurance — not raw model capability — are now the main bottleneck, requiring explicit quality standards, evaluation frameworks and feedback loops.

unique_angles.point: Liability ownership, permissions and tacit company-specific standards remain the hardest unsolved pieces.

top_stories.title: Google pushes Gemini into Pixel 11 as app hits 1 billion users
points: The Gemini app crossed 1 billion users, Google's fastest-growing product ever.
Pixel 11 ships with the Tensor G6 chip and Gemini handling multi-step tasks across 40+ apps, plus real-time video and audio translation and new voice capabilities.

items.title: Gamgee commercializes AI-designed cancer vaccines for dogs
points: The Y Combinator startup grew out of Paul Conyngham using ChatGPT, AlphaFold (DeepMind's protein-structure prediction model) and a custom mRNA vaccine to shrink his dog Rosie's tumors after conventional treatment failed.
Gamgee runs design, treatment and monitoring end-to-end, with first trials in Australia and cases accepted globally.
Sam Altman met Conyngham in March and encouraged him to start the company; the mutation-matched approach hints at eventual human applications.

items.title: Why your AI outputs feel dumb
points: Most users hand AI the final polished step instead of the research and ideation stages where it performs best.
Reframe tasks so AI does prep — research, brainstorming, wide exploration — while you handle cutting, editing and judging fit.
Tell the model upfront what format you work in (spreadsheet, Word doc, slide deck) so output lands where you finish work.

items.title: Turn customer feedback into 100 ad hooks
points: Feed 10-20 customer comments into ChatGPT and have it build a CSV of pain points, frustrating moments, desired outcomes and objections.
Generate a second CSV converting each pain point into headline, call-to-action and image-prompt ideas, then hand-pick the strongest angles.
Only after the manual output is solid, have ChatGPT scaffold a reusable app that reads the CSV and saves generated images via an OpenRouter API key (a service routing requests to many AI models).

items.title: Video and context tooling: Preview, Click, Infisical
points: Preview launched as a single workspace for video teams — storyboarding, generating, directing, comparing model outputs and keeping characters/locations consistent across shots.

Click added live context via MCP connections (Model Context Protocol, a plugin-style standard for feeding tools and data to AI), including YouTube transcripts, LinkedIn reactions, flight fares and financial data.
Infisical sandboxes Claude and other agents behind fake API keys, with a proxy swapping in real credentials only as requests leave the agent environment.

items.title: Training-data and licensing shifts
points: Amazon/Twitch will use streamer content to train generative AI by default unless creators explicitly opt out.
Apple is negotiating nine-figure (at least $100M) multiyear deals to pay publishers when Siri AI uses their content.

items.title: Governance and AI security
points: Demis Hassabis reportedly pitched a U.S.-led AI oversight body weeks before stepping down as DeepMind CEO to become Alphabet chief scientist — framed by some as a PR move for Google's stock.
Dream Security documented an autonomous multi-agent system that mapped and compromised Asian government entities over four days.

items.title: Anthropic to watermark all Claude output under EU rules
points: Anthropic will digitally watermark 100% of Claude-generated content to meet EU transparency requirements, tagging any output Claude touches.
The label applies indiscriminately — a blog post merely spellchecked by Claude gets flagged as AI-generated, even if a human wrote 99% of it.
OpenAI and Google committed to similar EU rules and already watermark images and audio.

items.title: Build an AI agent team instead of buying SaaS
points: One engineer replaced 20+ SaaS subscriptions at a 50-person business by creating per-workflow agent inboxes with the Nylas CLI.

Setup: install Nylas CLI, authenticate with an API key, create dedicated agent addresses (renewals@, invoices@), set rules limiting what each agent can act on, then hand the roster to Claude or another coding agent in one prompt.

items.title: DeepMind model translates American Sign Language to text
points: Google DeepMind released a model that converts ASL into text.

items.title: Microsoft ships MAI-Thinking-1 and MAI-Image-2.6
points: MAI-Thinking-1 is a cost-efficient reasoning model aimed at enterprise coding, math and knowledge work.
MAI-Image-2.6 reached #2 on the text-to-image Arena leaderboard, ahead of Google and Meta entries.

items.title: AI-generated production code fails most enterprise hardening tests
points: CData tested Claude Code building an MCP server across 8 enterprise-critical dimensions (OAuth token lifecycle, large-dataset behavior and more) and the generated code failed 7 of 8; expert guidance helped but not always enough.
Safe MCP servers force a tradeoff between agent flexibility (open SQL generation) and tight constraints (typed, pre-approved queries), requiring explicit permission-model decisions.
Specula, which uses formal specifications (TLA+ machine-checkable logical proofs), finds concurrency bugs but still can't verify that module-level guarantees compose into system-level guarantees.

items.title: Nvidia's 'synthetic hyperscaler' play
points: Nvidia is vertically integrating hardware, software and financing into a self-contained AI platform — like AWS but specialized for AI compute — raising switching costs for customers eyeing rival ASIC accelerators (custom purpose-built chips).

headlines: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 reaches frontier-level performance at 60% cheaper than competitors like OpenAI's Sol and Anthropic's Fable, with version 4.7 promised in 3-4 weeks.
Gamgee, a Y Combinator startup founded after a dog survived personalized AI-designed cancer vaccine, is now commercializing custom mRNA treatments for canine tumors.
AI coding platform Lovable raised $400M at $13.3B valuation, more than doubling its prior December valuation amid strong demand for no-code development tools.
Google's Gemini app hit 1 billion users, becoming the company's fastest-growing product ever, while Pixel 11 devices embed AI deeper with new voice and task capabilities.
DeepSeek quietly launched V4 Pro at just $0.44/$0.87 per 1M tokens with frontier-comparable benchmarks, intensifying competition on cost.

sections.title: 1. SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 Reshapes the Frontier
points: Grok 4.6 scored 61 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index, passing GPT-5.6 Sol and approaching Anthropic's Fable 5 (62) and Opus 5 (63).
Pricing of $2/$6 per 1M tokens (tokens are units of text/code the model processes) undercuts frontier competitors by 60%, forcing rivals to reconsider pricing and release timelines.
Elon Musk declared it 'objectively No. 1 when considering intelligence, speed & cost' and teased Grok 4.7 arriving in 3-4 weeks with claims it will 'exceed all current models.'
The shift from punchline to serious threat signals pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic—particularly with the Cursor/xAI partnership already showing collaborative strength.

sections.title: 2. Personalized AI Cancer Treatment Goes Commercial
points: Gamgee emerged from Paul Conyngham's rescue of his dog Rosie using ChatGPT, AlphaFold, and a custom mRNA vaccine that reduced tumors after conventional treatments failed.
The startup is conducting first trials in Australia and accepting cases globally, managing design, treatment, and monitoring end-to-end for custom dog cancer vaccines.
Sam Altman met with Conyngham in March and encouraged him to build a company, validating the real-world impact of applying AI to biotech at individual scale.
While focused on dogs, the model hints at broader potential for personalized cancer treatments in humans, with AI as the accelerant for mutation-matched drug design.

sections.title: 3. How to Stop Getting Dumb AI Outputs
points: Most frustrated users blame the AI model but are actually using it backwards: they hand it the final polished verb instead of the early research and ideation steps where AI excels.
Reframe tasks so AI does prep work (research, brainstorming, wider exploration) and you handle the last verb—cutting, editing, judging fit—where human expertise matters most.
Tell AI upfront what format you work in (spreadsheet, Word doc, slide deck) so outputs land where you finish work, reducing hand-off friction and rework.
The core insight: research, testing, and cutting are where AI does best work and where you can steer effectively; skipping those steps almost guarantees disappointing results.

sections.title: 4. Turn Customer Feedback Into 100 Ad Hooks
points: Extract 10–20 customer comments, have ChatGPT create a CSV with pain points, frustrating moments, desired outcomes, and objections for each comment.
Generate a second CSV turning each pain point into ad headline, call-to-action, and image prompt ideas; manually review and pick angles that resonate.

Once you settle on good output, ask ChatGPT to scaffold a reusable app that reads the CSV, generates ads, and saves images in folders via an OpenRouter API key (a service that routes requests to multiple AI models).
Key lesson: do the task manually first, iterate until output is solid, then automate; don't try to automate 100 things at launch.

sections.title: Grok 4.6: A Cost-Effective Frontier Model
points: Grok 4.6 ranks among frontier-level models, matching OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and trailing only Claude Opus 5 and Fable 5 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

Cost-effectiveness is the key differentiator: Grok 4.6 maintains the same cost per task as its predecessor Grok 4.5, making it comparable to open-source Chinese models despite its frontier performance.

issues.subject: Claude Chrome Cowork 🌐, Grok 4.6🚀, DeepSeek v4-Pro-0813 🧠

headlines: Anthropic upgraded Claude in Chrome with a full Cowork session in the side panel that saves conversations across devices, while Grok 4.6 now matches GPT-5.6 Sol on benchmarks and is available in Cursor and via API.
DeepSeek released V4-Pro-0813 model at $0.435 per 1M input tokens and $0.87 per 1M output tokens (roughly 1/10th the price of comparable models), outperforming Opus 4.8 on multiple benchmarks.
Microsoft launched MAI-Thinking-1, a cost-efficient reasoning model for enterprise workloads, and MAI-Image-2.6 reached #2 on the text-to-image Arena leaderboard.

Enterprise AI adoption is shifting from AI-as-assistant toward agentic delegation (autonomous agents handling tasks), with highest-usage firms generating 10x more output tokens per user than typical firms.

sections.title: 1. Model Pricing & Performance Shifts
points: DeepSeek V4-Pro-0813 costs $0.435/$0.87 per 1M tokens (input/output), undercutting major competitors by an order of magnitude while matching or beating Opus 4.8 on coding, benchmarking, and automation tasks.
Grok 4.6 now equals GPT-5.6 Sol performance on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; available immediately in Cursor, Grok Build, and via API with 2x free usage for the first week.

Microsoft's MAI-Thinking-1 targets cost-efficient enterprise reasoning for coding, math, and knowledge work; MAI-Image-2.6 reached second place on Arena leaderboard, ahead of Google and Meta offerings.

sections.title: 2. Enterprise AI Execution Overtaking Experimentation
points: OpenAI studies show enterprise adoption moving from assistance (where AI helps humans) toward agentic delegation (where AI autonomously completes work with human oversight).
Highest-usage firms consume 10x more output tokens per active user and adopt connected tools and workflows more frequently, indicating shift toward multi-step autonomous work.

Verification and quality assurance are now the primary adoption constraints—companies need systems to define quality standards, evaluate ongoing performance, and feedback loops; tacit standards and company-specific evaluation frameworks remain harder problems than raw capability.

sections.title: 3. Production Readiness Gaps in AI-Generated Systems
points: CData tested Claude Code building an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server across 8 enterprise-critical dimensions (OAuth token lifecycle, large dataset behavior, etc.) and found the AI-generated code failed on 7 of 8; expert guidance helped but wasn't always sufficient.

MCP server safety requires tradeoffs between agent flexibility (open SQL generation) and tight constraints (typed, pre-approved queries); building production-safe connectors requires explicit architectural decisions about permission models.

Specula, an automated bug-finding system using formal specifications (TLA+ logical proofs), can find concurrency bugs in system code but still cannot verify whether individual module guarantees compose into system-level guarantees—a fundamental unsolved problem.

sections.title: 4. Infrastructure & Platform Consolidation
points: Nvidia is building a vertically integrated 'synthetic hyperscaler' (a self-contained infrastructure platform combining hardware, software, and financing)—similar to cloud providers like AWS but specialized for AI hardware, making it difficult for customers to switch to competing accelerators (ASICs).

Enterprise AI hiring and deployment is bottlenecked by verification systems, not capability; companies struggle with defining quality, liability ownership, permissions, and self-improving feedback loops across agentic systems.
